title: “which vail is done away in Christ” (2 Corinthians 3:14) — Tischendorf’s Greek has a word meaning “because” and adds “this very day”
summary: The KJV ends 2 Corinthians 3:14 with “which vail is done away in Christ”. Two printed Greek editions link the clause differently. The older received text has which; the later edited text has because or that.
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 3:14: “But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.” Greek New Testament (later edited edition) 2 Corinthians 3:14: ἀλλὰ ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν. ἄχρι γὰρ τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας τὸ αὐτὸ κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τῇ ἀναγνώσει τῆς παλαιᾶς διαθήκης μένει μὴ ἀνακαλυπτόμενον, ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται· Greek New Testament (older received text, printed here without accents) 2 Corinthians 3:14: αλλ επωρωθη τα νοηματα αυτων αχρι γαρ της σημερον το αυτο καλυμμα επι τη αναγνωσει της παλαιας διαθηκης μενει μη ανακαλυπτομενον ο τι εν χριστω καταργειται Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/47/3/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/47/3/.
reasoning: The older edition links which to the veil being removed. The later edition links the clause as an explanation involving its removal in Christ.
scope: The finding concerns the clause link at 2 Corinthians 3:14 only. The earlier wording about this very day is outside the finding. This compares two printed Greek New Testament editions served by bolls.life. The older received text agrees with the KJV here; the later edited text differs. Full edition names are in Sources. The two editions do not provide a full review of ancient copies or establish which wording came first. Other small spelling and word-order differences are outside this finding.

title: “our care for you” (2 Corinthians 7:12) — Tischendorf’s Greek has “your care for us”
summary: At 2 Corinthians 7:12, the KJV describes “our care for you”. Two printed Greek editions differ: the older received text agrees, while the later edited text has your care for us.
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 7:12: “Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.” Greek New Testament (later edited edition) 2 Corinthians 7:12: ἄρα εἰ καὶ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, οὐκ ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικήσαντος οὐδὲ ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικηθέντος, ἀλλ’ ἕνεκεν τοῦ φανερωθῆναι τὴν σπουδὴν ὑμῶν τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ. Greek New Testament (older received text, printed here without accents) 2 Corinthians 7:12: αρα ει και εγραψα υμιν ουχ εινεκεν του αδικησαντος ουδε εινεκεν του αδικηθεντος αλλ εινεκεν του φανερωθηναι την σπουδην ημων την υπερ υμων προς υμας ενωπιον του θεου Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/47/7/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/47/7/.
reasoning: The pronouns reverse the direction of care. One names the writers' care for the Corinthians; the other names the Corinthians' care for the writers. The closing words about God's sight agree.
scope: The finding concerns the care pronouns at 2 Corinthians 7:12 only. It does not imply a different historical occasion. title: “comforted in your comfort” (2 Corinthians 7:13) — Tischendorf’s Greek has “our comfort” and starts a new sentence
summary: The KJV begins 2 Corinthians 7:13 with “Therefore we were comforted in your comfort”. The older of two printed Greek editions agrees. The later edited text has our comfort after a printed sentence break.
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 7:13: “Therefore we were comforted in your comfort: yea, and exceedingly the more joyed we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.” Greek New Testament (later edited edition) 2 Corinthians 7:13: διὰ τοῦτο παρακεκλήμεθα. ἐπὶ δὲ τῇ παρακλήσει ἡμῶν περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον ἐχάρημεν ἐπὶ τῇ χαρᾷ Τίτου, ὅτι ἀναπέπαυται τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ πάντων ὑμῶν· Greek New Testament (older received text, printed here without accents) 2 Corinthians 7:13: δια τουτο παρακεκλημεθα επι τη παρακλησει υμων περισσοτερως δε μαλλον εχαρημεν επι τη χαρα τιτου οτι αναπεπαυται το πνευμα αυτου απο παντων υμων Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/47/7/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/47/7/.
reasoning: Both the pronoun and the printed sentence division differ. The older edition links the Corinthians' comfort to the writers' comfort. The later edition places their own comfort alongside greater joy at Titus's refreshment.
scope: The finding concerns the comfort pronoun and sentence break at 2 Corinthians 7:13. The punctuation belongs to the printed edition, not every ancient copy. title: “whereof ye had notice before” (2 Corinthians 9:5) — Tischendorf’s Greek has “promised beforehand”
summary: At 2 Corinthians 9:5, the KJV describes a gift “whereof ye had notice before”. The older of two printed Greek editions has announced beforehand; the later edited text has promised beforehand.
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 9:5: “Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof ye had notice before, that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.” Greek New Testament (later edited edition) 2 Corinthians 9:5: ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἡγησάμην παρακαλέσαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἵνα προέλθωσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ προκαταρτίσωσιν τὴν προεπηγγελμένην εὐλογίαν ὑμῶν, ταύτην ἑτοίμην εἶναι οὕτως ὡς εὐλογίαν, μὴ ὡς πλεονεξίαν. Greek New Testament (older received text, printed here without accents) 2 Corinthians 9:5: αναγκαιον ουν ηγησαμην παρακαλεσαι τους αδελφους ινα προελθωσιν εις υμας και προκαταρτισωσιν την προκατηγγελμενην ευλογιαν υμων ταυτην ετοιμην ειναι ουτως ως ευλογιαν και μη ωσπερ πλεονεξιαν Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/47/9/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/47/9/.
reasoning: Announcing a gift in advance differs from promising it in advance. This is the compared verb wording, without a new claim about related dictionary forms.
scope: The finding concerns the announced/promised verb at 2 Corinthians 9:5 only. Neither reading is claimed for every ancient copy. title: “minister bread … multiply … increase” (2 Corinthians 9:10) — Tischendorf’s Greek has future-tense verbs
summary: At 2 Corinthians 9:10, the KJV expresses a wish about God's provision, agreeing with the older printed Greek edition. The later edited text uses future forms: will supply, multiply and increase.
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 9:10: “Now he that ministereth seed to the sower both minister bread for your food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;)” Greek New Testament (later edited edition) 2 Corinthians 9:10: ὁ δὲ ἐπιχορηγῶν σπέρμα τῷ σπείροντι καὶ ἄρτον εἰς βρῶσιν χορηγήσει καὶ πληθυνεῖ τὸν σπόρον ὑμῶν καὶ αὐξήσει τὰ γενήματα τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὑμῶν· Greek New Testament (older received text, printed here without accents) 2 Corinthians 9:10: ο δε επιχορηγων σπερμα τω σπειροντι και αρτον εις βρωσιν χορηγησαι και πληθυναι τον σπορον υμων και αυξησαι τα γεννηματα της δικαιοσυνης υμων Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/47/9/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/47/9/.
reasoning: The older edition's forms support the KJV's wish about God providing these things. The later edition states what God will do. The KJV clause uses the third person; it is not direct speech addressed to God.
scope: The finding concerns the three compared verbs at 2 Corinthians 9:10 only. This compares two printed Greek New Testament editions served by bolls.life. The older received text agrees with the KJV here; the later edited text differs. Full edition names are in Sources. title: “which the Lord hath given us” (2 Corinthians 10:8) — Tischendorf’s Greek has no “us” and a future verb for “boast”
summary: KJV 2 Corinthians 10:8 has “though I should boast somewhat more … which the Lord hath given us”. The Textus Receptus text served prints καυχησωμαι [I should boast] and ημιν [to us] after εδωκεν ο κυριος; Tischendorf’s text prints καυχήσομαι [I shall boast] and has no ημιν.
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 10:8: “For though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord hath given us for edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed:” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 2 Corinthians 10:8: ἐάν τε γὰρ περισσότερόν τι καυχήσομαι περὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας ἡμῶν, ἧς ἔδωκεν ὁ κύριος εἰς οἰκοδομὴν καὶ οὐκ εἰς καθαίρεσιν ὑμῶν, οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσομαι, Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) 2 Corinthians 10:8: εαν τε γαρ και περισσοτερον τι καυχησωμαι περι της εξουσιας ημων ης εδωκεν ο κυριος ημιν εις οικοδομην και ουκ εις καθαιρεσιν υμων ουκ αισχυνθησομαι Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/47/10/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/47/10/.
reasoning: Two small differences in one verse: a subjunctive “should boast” against a future “shall boast”, and a pronoun “us” present in the TR text but absent from Tischendorf’s. The authority is “ours” in both; only the TR text says the Lord gave it “to us”.
scope: T applies at 2 Corinthians 10:8 only. The difference is between Greek editions: the Textus Receptus text served agrees with the KJV and Tischendorf’s text does not. This record does not say which reading is original, and two digital editions are not a survey of manuscripts. The Greek New Testament wording is Tischendorf’s eighth edition as served by bolls.life (TISCH), compared with the Textus Receptus text served there (TR); neither is a critical apparatus. Only the words named are compared; other small spelling or word-order differences in the verse are not claimed.
